newsitem.title: UK: BT says can't rule out new MCI deal.
newsitem.headline: BT says can't rule out new MCI deal.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Friday that it could not rule out the possibility of re-negotiating its around $24 billion merger with MCI Communications Corp but said speculation at this stage was premature.
"At this stage we are simply looking at the figures and anything beyond that is premature," a company spokesman said.
BT's shares slid 25.5p to 452p in early trade, after MCI issued a profit warning late on Thursday.
"We do understand the significance and we haven't ruled out re-negotiation (of the deal)," the BT spokesman added. But he said the situation was "pretty complex".
"We're not going beyond that at this stage," he said.
MCI's management has told BT that the present outlook for the results of U.S. carrier, America's second biggest long-distance operator, is worse than market expectations.

"Initial discussions have been taking place with the MCI management regarding this trading situation and BT will be holding further discussions with MCI management in order fully to understand the reasons for, and extent of, the changes in MCI's prospects," BT said in a statement.

MCI said on Thursday it would forge ahead with the heavy investments it has been making to break into local telephone markets despite its efforts being hampered by what it calls "anti-competitive behaviour" from dominant local rivals. Thus earnings in the second half of 1997 and next year would be below expectations, it said.
BT said forecasts of local market losses were more than twice of previous expectations. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
